- Kept "made the volunteers feel differently": idiomatic.
- Kept "the influence of climate change".
- Only "the change of seasons" is reported.

z27 (Chongqing, underwater data centers), source is Scientific American, "China Is Putting Data Centers in the Ocean":
- These figures match the source: seawater pumped through radiators on the back of the servers; about 40% of electricity spent on cooling; "at least 30% less electricity" from the CAICT assessment; wind supplying 97% (consistent with "more than 95%").
- I could not verify "December 2022" for Hainan or "reduce land usage by 80%". Other reports say over 90%, but nothing definite, so I left both.
- Kept "show its promise to create": "promise" can also be read as potential.
- Kept "The act not only helps … but also could set": unidiomatic but not wrong. "This move" would be smoother; not reported.
- Kept "It forces countries to look for new ways to solve the big problem".

z28 (Chengdu, Forest Listeners, Google Arts & Culture / DeepMind / WildMon, Nov 2025):
- The 1.2 million recordings figure matches one report.
- Kept "However, that is a big job.": the contrast connector works, and Q32 depends on "that".
- Kept the missing commas before "but" in [1.2] and [1.4]: optional for short clauses.
- Kept "train AI to tell what animals they are by their sounds": loose pronoun, but understandable.

z29 (Chengdu, sleep):
- Kept "reducing pains": plural "pains" exists, as in "aches and pains"; "pain" would be better. Not reported.
- Kept "start their job at a certain time": "start work" would be more idiomatic; borderline, not reported.
- Kept "moved … to the city to work in the factories": generic "the" is acceptable.
- Kept "light bulb in 1879" (Edison, the standard school fact), "Starting in the 18th century" (Industrial Revolution) and "alarm clocks … 1930s and 1940s": all plausible and consistent with each other.
- Kept the abrupt switch to imperative tips in ¶4: matches the paper, and it is a style matter, not an error.
